print_process.orientation: Z vertical; flat undersides on build plate
print_process.joint_support_policy: No support material in any joint gap; intended no-support profile used for the assembly check

joint_motion_mesh_sample.method: nearest-vertex spacing between separately exported part meshes after Z rotations
joint_motion_mesh_sample.result: pass for the sampled CAD poses; this is not a substitute for a physical print test

automatic_support_slice.result: informational; supports are not used for the joint gaps

limitations: No physical PLA print and break-in test was possible in this environment. The 0.50 mm radial clearance, 0.60 mm vertical receiver-to-tail-base gap, captive keeper geometry, and +/-20 degree poses were checked in CAD/STL and by slicing, but printer calibration can still cause a tight or fused joint.

The automatic-support slice reports general print-stability/overhang warnings and generates support elsewhere on the dinosaur. The intended assembly was also successfully sliced with the supplied no-support profile and contains no support feature markers; no support is required inside the joint gaps. A brim may be useful for bed adhesion.
The nearest-spacing motion check is a mesh-vertex sampling check, not a certified continuous collision proof. It found positive spacing at the neutral and +/-20 degree samples for all three joints.
